name: Recruit utilities (“smurfs”)
note: The blue work uniform issued at recruit training. Sailors called it the smurfs. This is the first uniform in the record.

name: Navy PT uniform
note: The Navy physical training uniform.

name: EODMU-5 PT
context: Command PT gear, EOD Mobile Unit Five
note: Command physical training gear from EOD Mobile Unit Five.

name: JCSE PT
context: Command PT gear, Joint Communications Support Element
note: Command physical training gear from the Joint Communications Support Element.

name: EODMU-5 organizational (cargo diver shorts)
context: Organizational clothing, EOD Mobile Unit Five
note: EOD Mobile Unit Five organizational clothing: the tan shirt worn with olive cargo diver shorts.

name: Dungarees
note: Blue denim trousers and a chambray shirt, the ordinary working uniform before the blue digital camouflage. Shown second because that is the order given. The years are not entered.

name: Utilities
note: Listed in the record as its own uniform, separate from dungarees and from the later camouflage. Which utility pattern is not further described.

name: Coveralls
note: One-piece shipboard coveralls, the practical uniform for work in a machinery space or on deck. Associated with sea duty. The years are not entered.

name: Blue camouflage (NWU Type I)
note: The Navy's blue digital working uniform, the Type I, often called blueberries. Shown here because the record says blue camouflage. Confirm that this is the pattern, and add the years.

name: Green camouflage (NWU Type III)
note: The Navy’s green digital working uniform, the Type III.

name: Peanut butters
context: Navy Service Uniform, E-6 and below
note: The Navy Service Uniform that replaced the Johnny Cash and the summer whites at the end of 2010. Sailors called it peanut butters for the khaki shirt. Black trousers and a black garrison cap went with it. Worn until the chief's uniforms on 16 September 2014. A chief's khaki has khaki trousers, not these black ones.

name: Chief’s working khaki
note: Making chief replaces the jumper uniforms with chief's uniforms: service khaki, dress blue, and dress white among them. The record says nearly all of them were worn, and dinner dress was not.

name: Winter blue (“Johnny Cash”)
note: The black winter working uniform, nicknamed for the singer because it was black shirt and black trousers. Worn in the order given. The years are not entered.

name: Summer white
note: A white working uniform for hot climates, simpler than dress whites. The years are not entered.

name: Service dress blue (jumper)
note: The Navy dress blue jumper, with the broad collar and white piping, for sailors below chief. After 2014 the chief's dress blue is a coat, not this jumper.

name: Service dress white (jumper)
note: The white jumper, worn for inspections and ceremonies in summer whites season. The chief's version, after 2014, is a different coat.

name: Chief’s summer white
note: The chief’s summer white uniform.

name: Chief’s service dress blue
note: The chief’s dress blue coat. The photograph in this case is this uniform.

name: Chief’s service dress white
note: The chief’s dress white uniform.

name: Green camouflage (Woodland BDU)
note: Listed after the blue camouflage and before the desert pattern. The Navy Working Uniform Type III, the other green pattern, is shown with the work uniforms.

name: Desert camouflage
note: Desert camouflage worn with the Iraq tours. The 2006 and 2009 deployments are the likely years. The exact pattern, often the three-color desert uniform in that era, is not confirmed.

name: Army Combat Uniform (recorded as AWU)
note: The record says Army AWUs for the individual-augmentee tour. The Army uniform of 2008–2009 was the Army Combat Uniform in the gray-green digital pattern. AWU is kept as the name in the record so it can be corrected.

name: Multicam (Army OCP)
note: The camouflage worn with the joint communications deployments to Afghanistan. The record places it after the Army uniform and before the chief's uniforms.
